on 16 June, 2021

Author: Tirthankar Ghosh
Bench: Tirthankar Ghosh

16.06.2021 In The High Court At Calcutta
Item No.11 Criminal Revisional Jurisdiction
Ct.No.34
 dc.
 C.R.R. 1112 of 1994
 (Via Video Conference)
 M/s. Usha Tea Co. & Anr.
 versus
 The Corporation of Calcutta & Ors.
 In Re: An Application filed under Sections 401 and 482 read
 with Section 397 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
Mr. Arindam Jana ...
For the Petitioners.
Mr. Anindya Sundar Chatterjee,
Mr. Goutam Dinda ...

For the K.M.C.
 Md. Anwar Hossain,
 Ms. Sreyashee Biswas ... For the State.
The records reflect that the genesis of the case is in the  year 1982.
The petitioner no.1 is a partnership firm and the  petitioner no.2 is partner of the said firm.

The learned Senior  Municipal Magistrate, Calcutta in Case No. 4D of 1982  convicted the petitioner no.2 being the partner of the said  firm under the relevant provisions of Prevention of Food  Adulteration Act, 1954 read with Section 7 of the said Act  and sentenced the petitioner no.2 to suffer rigorous  imprisonment for six months and pay fine of Rs.1000/-, in M/S. Usha Tea Co. & Anr vs The Corporation Of Calcutta & Ors on 16 June, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26887430/
1  default, to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one month.

entities.text: M/S. Usha Tea Co. & Anr vs The Corporation Of Calcutta & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The  petitioners challenged this judgment and order passed in the  said case before the learned Sessions Judge, VIIIth Bench,
 City Sessions Court, Calcutta in Criminal Appeal No. 23 of  1991.

entities.text:
Sessions Judge, VIIIth Bench,
 City Sessions Court, Calcutta
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The learned Sessions Judge after appreciating the  evidence, affirmed the judgement and order of conviction  passed by the learned Senior Municipal Magistrate, Calcutta.
2  The order of appeal was passed on 19.04.1994 and against the said order, the petitioners approached this Court in the present revisional application on 10.06.1994.
The revisional application has been pending since then.

Having regard to the time so consumed by the court in considering and disposing of the revisional application, I am of the view that the petitioner no.2 has suffered from mental agony because of the sentence so imposed by the learned Senior Municipal Magistrate, Calcutta for almost 39 years.
Having regard to the said fact, I am of the view that it would be of no consequence if the petitioner no.2, after such a long time, is sent to the correctional home.

Under such circumstances, I exercise my power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and direct the petitioner no.2 to deposit a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with the learned Senior Municipal Magistrate,
Calcutta by 22.06.2021.
 Let the matter be made part heard.
